target_boundary: projects/ui-prototyping-studio docs plus sampled live backend code under backend/src/modules/ui-prototyping-studio and backend/src/cli/studio.ts

reader_contract.target_public: Local private project explanation for a person who wants to understand and try the UI Prototyping Studio tool.
assumed_knowledge: Basic idea of making a UI mockup
No prior knowledge of this repository
reader_contract.reader_reward: Understand what the tool is, what a first session feels like, how the workflow moves, how it was made, and which examples to try.

must_not_start_with: proof metrics before the reader understands the workflow
opening_contract.failure_message: If the page reads like a product pitch or file inventory before explaining how to use the tool, the reader contract failed.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: AI can generate and revise interfaces, but durable changes remain visible, reversible, or explicitly confirmed.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It tells a new user why the studio asks them to look, choose, and accept instead of just generating a final answer.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not start with governance jargon before showing the user what they actually do.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The point where externally generated HTML enters the studio through the CLI.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It explains why generated HTML can come from Claude Code today and another engine later without changing the main workflow.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not treat generation as embedded in the studio core.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The deterministic core decision that admits or rejects a proposed UI change.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It explains the plain checkpoint where the studio says whether a proposed change is allowed to become a staged candidate.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not claim the AI proposal itself is replayable; the verdict is.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: Approve the intent first, then stage the candidate and accept the exact diff before it becomes head.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It explains why a user sees the proposed result before keeping it.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: SPEC.md, states.md, apply-and-stage.ts, accept-staged-revision.ts; lifecycle lane
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not collapse staging and recording into one apply action.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A per-component before/after measurement based on od-id structure, not on declared task labels.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It lets a user compare what actually changed instead of trusting a vague summary.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not describe it as proof of human understanding or preference.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: Most actions can be undone through append-only history; export remains the explicit irreversible edge.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It explains why trying a faster automated pass can still be safe enough for local exploration.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not use reversibility to justify unconfirmed handoff export.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: I want to understand what this tool is before seeing implementation details.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: The studio helps a person try UI ideas with Claude Code, inspect the HTML in a browser, comment on components, and keep or revert revisions.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: Starting the presentation with a usable mental model instead of proof metrics.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: I want to know what I would do in a first session.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Ask, register variants, preview, choose a baseline, annotate, synthesize, stage, accept or revert, and export when ready.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: Trying the tool without getting lost in local vocabulary.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: I want to know how it was made after I understand the workflow.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: A CLI adapter, browser preview, orchestration core, domain state machine, admission checker, artifact store, and tests cooperate around one local loop.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: Connecting the user's actions to the implementation without making the deck feel like a code audit.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: I want to know where Claude Code fits.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Claude Code makes the HTML proposal; the studio records, previews, checks, stages, and saves it.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: Avoiding the mistaken idea that the studio itself is an embedded model.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: I want to know the careful parts without being buried in caveats.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Browser evidence shows what happened on screen, but not whether the design is good or trusted; deeper identity and scoring work remain future layers.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: Using the tool honestly while learning what it can and cannot prove.

evidence: README.md describes the product as accountable UI exploration: generate a bounded set of variants, select a baseline, annotate, synthesize, approve, apply, append a revision manifest, and hand off.
README.md states the backend is runnable through the studio CLI and preview surface.
SPEC.md scopes the release to the L0 -> L2 survival/trust floor.
inference: The strongest product positioning is not generic UI generation; it is accountable AI-assisted UI revision.

evidence: SPEC.md and states.md define variantCount 1..3, baseline selection, comments, mutation batches, revisions, and session states.
models.ts includes StudioSessionState values through RevisionApplied, RevisionRecorded, and SessionCompleted.
admission.ts implements an od-id attributed scope validator and honest per-od-id diff.
inference: The most valuable properties are reversibility, bounded exploration, source-backed intent capture, and visible admission.

evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names Claude Code, studio CLI, operating skill, orchestration core, session store, and studio preview.
backend/src/cli/studio.ts implements session, prompt, variants, baseline, comment, synthesize, approve, apply, accept, discard, preview, revert, pending, watch, cycle, revisions, and handoff export.
backend/package.json exposes build, check, studio, test, test:e2e, and test:skill scripts.
inference: The component map reads as a local-first product kernel that could later accept other generation engines without changing the core contract.

evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md states interface depends on application, application depends on domain, infrastructure implements ports, and domain depends on nothing.
apply-and-stage.ts depends on current HTML resolution, admission validation, artifact content, and the session store.
accept-staged-revision.ts commits staged content, appends a revision, saves session state, and clears staged candidate.
inference: The load-bearing internal dependency is the path from CLI command to orchestration use case to pure gate to append-only store.

evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md says Claude Code is the generation engine and the CLI is the seam; no MCP server, no web SPA, no API key in the MVP.
INTEGRATION.md says host apps drive the CLI by shelling out, parsing stdout JSON, and checking the exit code.
backend/package.json lists Fastify and Playwright-related development dependencies.
inference: A future hosted product would need to replace the local trust boundary with explicit auth, multi-user state, and engine adapters.

evidence: README.md and INTEGRATION.md list the loop: session open, prompt submit, variants register, baseline select or commit, comment add, synthesize, approve, apply, accept, revisions, handoff export.
run-cycle.ts implements AUTO exploit/explore cycles that gate candidates and auto-accept the top admitted score with reversibility.
preview e2e tests cover annotation into pending comments.
inference: The product has two useful modes: supervised human-in-the-loop revision and reversible automated cycling.

evidence: states.md defines the deterministic StudioSessionState sequence and the RevisionApplied staged preview state.
PLAN-NEXT.md says post-build hardening landed with unit 61/61, Playwright e2e 13/13, tsc clean, export confirm in core, preview accept/discard/revert, cycle score validation, and cycle ceiling.
governance.spec.ts tests export confirmation, revert restoration, and append-only auto-accept reversibility.
inference: The live product is best described as an MVP-grade local control loop, not the full L4-L6 research vision.

evidence: CRAFT.md and the ledger name ergonomics unproven, fixture or validator calibration, identity types, failure states, and other gaps.
admission.ts carries a note that the V3 alignment key is brittle to legitimate structural reordering and production needs more robust node identity plus real CSS cascade.
SPEC.md defers L4 identity/DNA, L5 fitness, and L6 human evidence/trust.
inference: The main product risk is overclaiming human trust or taste from automated browser evidence.
The main technical risk is relying too long on od-id scope attribution before deeper identity and CSS semantics are built.

evidence: x-ray library patterns used: dependency-boundary, lifecycle-stack, process-branch, evidence-inference-split.
x-ray library components used: shape.node, shape.boundary, shape.layer-panel, shape.risk-marker, connector.arrow, connector.branch, connector.feedback-loop, chart.timeline-strip, chart.risk-matrix.
inference: A static slide deck with layer toggles is enough because the target is a codebase/product explanation, not a live product demo.
